newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark edges lower in Europe, eyes on Buba meet.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark edges lower in Europe, eyes on Buba meet.

text.p: The dollar edged lower against the mark in morning Europe, backing off overnight highs just above 1.83 as it succumbed to some mark short-covering ahead of today's Bundesbank council meeting.
Dealers said trade was cautious ahead of the meeting amid expectations of pro mark comments from Bundesbank members and even some speculation of a switch to a variable repo rate.

"This talk has gone around before but it's highly unlikely we'll seen any change at all at the meeting, not before the summer recess," said Tom Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull.

Dealers said if the German authorities were that keen to stem mark weakness, a switch to a variable repo could send a powerful signal to the market by breaking the long-held perception of steady German interest rates.

But SGST's Rayner was mindful that the German economy still did not warrant a rate rise and a variable repo did not necessarily mean key interest rates would rise, a risk the Bundesbank was unlikely to take with the current climate of mark weakness.
By 0735 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.8233 marks, just above earlier session lows at 1.8220 but still short of the overnight 1.8315 and Wednesday's 71-month high of 1.8325 marks.

Any mark positive rhetoric from the German central bank today is seen having a limited impact as the market has become convinced of Germany's tolerance of the weaker mark. The Bundesbank's concern is with the pace of the dollar/mark rise rather than the level, said dealers.

"There's a bit of nervousness because there's the chance the press will catch some of the members on the way out and they might say something mark-positive, but that would be a short-term effect," said Robin Poynder, chief dealer at Charterhouse.
Mark short-covering also saw the German unit firm slightly on its European crosses in morning trade.
Mark/yen dipped from early highs, trading at 63.33/35 yen against 63.57 earlier and 63.47/49 late Wednesday in Europe.

Dollar/yen was firm, though steady below 116 yen. Dealers said there was some mild support from a downbeat Bank of Japan quarterly economic report, putting further into the background concerns of higher Japanese interest rates any time soon.
Although the Japanese economy continues to recover, its pace was moderate and is unlikely to gain significant momentum, said the BOJ report.
Dollar/yen was trading at 115.78/88, little changed from 115.73/78 late Wednesday.
Sterling, meantime, slipped back from Wednesday's over seven-year highs above 3.08 marks, steadying around 3.05 marks in morning trade.
Dealers said Bank of England governor Eddie George helped dampen enthusiasm for sterling/mark late Wednesday when he said some of the pound's recent rise was irrational and erratic.
By 0820 GMT, sterling/mark stood at 3.0491/01 against 3.0610/20 late Wednesday in Europe. The next focus for sterling was today's UK May and June trade data due at 0830 GMT.
